gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the $99.99 Amazfit Bip Max is rated for 10 days under Amazfit's heavy-use test (heart rate every minute, 24-hour wear). That is the cheapest model whose worst-case rating is close to two weeks, compared with 6 days for the Bip 6, which ChatGPT sold as the 'two-week' value pick.
standout_why: I compared it against The Gadgeteer's under-$200 list, which has the Bip 6, Active 2, Forerunner 165, Galaxy Watch FE and Fitbit Versa 4. None of them is the Bip Max, and the list gives only maker 'up to' battery figures. ChatGPT's answers showed the Bip Max card with 'up to 20 days' but no heavy-use figure. Our own current page has no Bip Max row. I couldn't open the Tom's Guide, Yahoo Tech or Android Central pages: Tom's Guide and Android Central came back truncated and Yahoo returned a 403. So I can't rule out that one of them mentions it.
decides: This keeps the Active Max ($169.99) as the safest pick for a real two weeks. Our page lists it at 13 days heavy, but I couldn't re-check that today because Amazfit rate-limited me. It moves the value slot from the Bip 6 ($79.99) to the Bip Max ($99.99): for $20 more, the heavy-use rating goes from 6 to 10 days. Every model priced today that is rated 14 days or more and costs under $200 is an Amazfit. Active 2 Round and Square are rated 10 days, The Gadgeteer gives the Forerunner 165 11 days, the Apple Watch SE 3 runs on hours, and Balance 2 and T-Rex 3 are over $200.

findings.note: From the spec list on Amazfit's UK page, because the US product page returned HTTP 429. Footnote: the heavy test is 24-hour wear with heart rate every 1 min, stress and breathing tracking, and 200 raise-to-wake events a day. The typical test is heart rate every 5 min, 150 notifications a day and three 30-min GPS workouts a week. Heavy use is half the typical figure (10/20). The same page lists iOS 15.0+ support. WhatsApp speech-to-text replies need Android 7+.
